review.title: Provider and URL security review
review.acceptance: A findings register exists at docs/SECURITY_REVIEW_PROVIDER_URL.md enumerating every finding across the five named classes -- SSRF, secret exposure, redirect handling, allowlist enforcement, and rights bypass -- each with a disposition of RESOLVED (with the commit and the test that now fails without the fix) or ACCEPTED (with the reason, the residual risk, and who accepted it). AN EMPTY REGISTER IS NOT A PASS. The register must state, per class, what was examined and by what method, so that 'no finding' is distinguishable from 'not looked for'; a class examined by reading alone must say so rather than implying a test covered it. Every RESOLVED entry needs a regression that fails against the pre-fix tree, because a security fix without a test that would have caught the bug is indistinguishable from a refactor. Every ACCEPTED entry that touches credentials, licensing or an irreversible production change is an escalation under control/policies.json escalation.humanOnly and may NOT be accepted by an agent; it is recorded as OPEN-ESCALATED and named in the handoff. Out of scope and to be listed as such rather than silently skipped: anything requiring a real licensed provider or live credentials (PL-0302, PL-0602), and the desktop sidecar trust boundary already ruled on in PL-0901 and reviewed under PL-0501.

The original clause, preserved verbatim in acceptanceSupersededAtClaim, was: 'SSRF, secret exposure, redirect, allowlist, and rights-bypass findings are resolved or explicitly accepted'. That sentence is satisfied by an agent reporting that it found nothing, which under invariant 8 is the shape of a fabricated gate rather than a passed one: the only two gates on this task are security-review and rights-review, both judgement gates, and neither has a command whose exit code can contradict a wrong answer. The amendment does not lower the bar or narrow the scope -- the same five classes, the same surface -- it makes the existing bar falsifiable, by requiring the method to be published alongside the conclusion and by refusing an empty register as evidence. If the reviewer considers a pre-claim acceptance amendment by the implementing lead improper even in the stricter direction, this is the record to point at, and the original clause is recoverable from the field above.

review.title: A real catalog metadata source
review.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
review.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at integrated head 645e58562dc0e2376f7395da19d0991a9899e972, exit 0, 17 of 17 and 0 cached, 2318 passed; catalog-ingestion now 117 cases across 8 files. THE COMMANDER'S LICENSING DECISION IS NOW IMPLEMENTED: Wikidata stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataProvider, which closes the first acceptance clause that round 44 correctly refused to claim. The port did not move -- wikidata.ts imports FROM provider.ts and nothing in the port imports back, and ingest, project, identity, freshness and safety never mention Wikidata -- which is what keeps the decision an INITIAL source choice rather than a shape baked into the seam. CAPABILITIES ARE DECLARED HONESTLY RATHER THAN OPTIMISTICALLY, each measured: providerSideSearch true; incrementalSince FALSE because WDQS's default graph binds nothing for schema:version or dateModified and the Action API that has them costs a measured 206 KB per entity, so changedSince is ignored entirely rather than silently approximated; reportsDeletions FALSE because deletions need a different API; maxPageSize 50, the number the source itself uses; and sourceRevision ALWAYS NULL, which is a real gap stated as one -- a consumer cannot tell whether a record changed between passes. Enumeration is keyset-paged on the numeric QID rather than OFFSET, because CirrusSearch hard-fails at offset 10,000, measured. THE CC0 / CC BY-SA DISTINCTION IS ENFORCED BY FOUR MECHANICAL CONTROLS, NOT DOCUMENTED: a frozen two-host set with construction refused if the operator's egress allowlist names anything else, so en.wikipedia.org in the policy yields NO provider; an entity-id pattern admitting only Q, P and L, with Commons M-ids refused by name; no SERVICE clause in any built query, asserted; and no request for P18, P154, P3383, sitelinks or extracts, with artwork always empty and unable to be otherwise. THE USER-AGENT OBLIGATION IS STRUCTURAL: the option stays required with no default, createWikidataProvider additionally refuses an agent string with no contact token or with a browser token by two separate named refusals, and a ts-expect-error test fails if a default is ever added -- a bad agent gets no provider rather than an IP block. RIGHTS MACHINERY ON REAL RECORDS: the rights register is required with no default and noRightsBasisEstablished must be passed BY NAME, so a default composition against real Wikidata publishes NOTHING, asserted over three recorded real films -- that is the correct outcome, not a bug. P6216 is read and not interpreted. The pre-parse media-address scan now has an untrusted writer behind it, since a Wikidata label is editable by anyone logged in and a vandalised title reading like a manifest URL is an ordinary string to the schema; the test is built from a real response with one label replaced. A FINDING THE IMPLEMENTER GOT BY WRITING THE TEST AND GETTING THE OTHER ANSWER: a rights reference carrying a contract URL is refused as media_address_in_catalog_payload rather than as a non-opaque reference, because the address scan runs first. ROUND 44'S TRIPWIRE FIRED AND WAS INVERTED RATHER THAN DELETED: the licensed-source set is frozen, holds only wikidata, throws on runtime mutation and licenses no keyed source, and a tmdb request is refused by name. LIVE TESTS ARE OUT OF THE GATE: wikidata.live.test.ts hits the real service, is excluded by the package vitest config, reachable only through a separate script, and was run deliberately -- 3 passed in 20.4s -- but is not what this gate rests on.

licensingDecision.obligationsThatFollow: Wikidata's structured data is CC0, but access is not unconditional: the Wikimedia User-Agent policy requires an informative User-Agent with contact information or the client may be IP-blocked without notice, and browser-impersonating agents are forbidden. That is why CatalogDocumentOptions.userAgent is required with no default, and it must stay that way. Text outside the main, property and lexeme namespaces is CC BY-SA rather than CC0, so the distinction has to survive into whatever is ingested.

review.title: An agent instruction file has provenance, or it is not an instruction
review.acceptance: Repository validation detects any AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md under a working directory that is not on an explicit, reviewed allowlist, and the authoritative instruction hierarchy is stated somewhere an agent reads before it starts. THE CONCRETE CASE: apps/web/AGENTS.md is GENERATED BY next dev and instructs agents to read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. Nothing acted on it, and it is almost certainly benign. The finding is not that file -- it is that framework tooling can write an instruction file into a directory agents treat as authoritative, which makes a dependency's postinstall a path into the control plane's instruction surface. Required: the allowlist names each legitimate instruction file and who owns it, so an unowned one is a validation failure rather than a judgement call; generated instruction files are either gitignored and removed or allowlisted after being read, and the choice is recorded per file; validation fails on an unexpected file rather than warning, because a warning in a passing run is not a control; a regression plants an unexpected AGENTS.md and observes the failure, since a detector nobody has seen fire is not known to work; and the instruction hierarchy is written down -- which file wins, and that nothing under node_modules is ever authoritative. WHAT THIS TASK MUST NOT DO: silently delete a file a framework needs, or treat allowlisting as review. An allowlisted generated file must have been READ by a human or an agent that reports what it says.
review.notes: Created 2026-09-18 on gpt-architect's round-46 instruction, reviewing PL-0702 at bbfaa5a997e6ee146271f26e5b2546b7e67e47d2. The reviewer also required, separately from the register dispositions, that no finding in docs/SECURITY_REVIEW_PROVIDER_URL.md remain at OPEN-OUT-OF-SURFACE, and that the deferral be carried by a real task with the proper owning surface rather than by a note. This one came out of the PL-0702 subagent flagging the file rather than acting on it, which is the behaviour the instruction-source boundary asks for; the reviewer agreed it is a real control-plane supply-chain surface and directed that it NOT block PL-0502. Lane is Coordination and preferredAgent was corrected from claude-infra to claude-lead at the claim: claude-infra does not advertise the Coordination lane, and the control plane refused the claim rather than silently substituting an agent, which is the behaviour allowAutomaticReviewerSubstitution=false exists for.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at integrated head a074b986e899ba8b91d018c4bb71f8c12089b608, exit 0, 15 of 15 and 0 cached, 2172 passed. THE FINDING IS THAT TWO OF THE THREE MEMBERS WERE ALREADY ENGINE-NEUTRAL AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED: engine_load_failed is exactly 'libmpv did not load' and names no engine, no library and no host. The gap was never a missing member; it was that the union was DOCUMENTED as three observed browser situations, so a native adapter author would reasonably conclude none applied and invent one. So this is a re-specification plus the missing detail channel, not a new member -- and adding libmpv_unavailable beside browser_unsupported was refused, because that would leave the union naming one engine's failure modes and one library's, which is the coupling the task exists to remove. 'The engine loaded and refused this source' was also refused: unavailability is decided once before any source, while a per-source refusal is per-candidate and feeds failover, and DESKTOP_PLAYBACK section 3 already owns it as PlayerRefusalCode on canPlay. That refusal is what satisfies the no-retryable constraint BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard. CONSTRAINT PROVEN IN THREE LAYERS: the reason set and the failure-kind set are disjoint and neither contains network_transient; the live route was traced -- an unavailability does reach classifyPlaybackFailure as ENGINE_ERROR and returns null because describePlaybackError of a non-shaka error yields category null and code null -- and the detail's code is a namespaced STRING precisely so an mpv number cannot be assigned where the classifier reads Shaka's scale; and the unavailability state path terminates at fatal without touching the scheduler. Five mutations were each confirmed to fail, including collapsing the missing-engine case onto browser_unsupported and building the error from a Shaka timeout.

review.title: An engine-unavailable reason that can say libmpv did not load
review.description: EngineUnavailableReason in apps/web/src/components/player/playback-controller.ts is Shaka-shaped. Its members describe a browser that cannot run the web engine, and browser_unsupported is a misnomer the moment the engine is a native library in a desktop shell rather than a script in a page. There is no member that means the native player failed to load. A NativePlayerAdapter would have to report a false reason or invent one locally, and either makes the failure less debuggable than the web path it sits beside.
review.notes: THE VOCABULARY, NOT A NEW MEMBER. Adding a libmpv_unavailable member beside browser_unsupported would leave the union naming one engine's failure modes and one library's, which is the same coupling one layer up. The question for the reviewer is whether the reason should describe WHAT FAILED in engine-neutral terms -- the engine could not be loaded, the platform cannot run this engine, the engine loaded and refused this source -- with the engine's own detail carried beside it rather than encoded in the member name. COUPLED TO PL-0904 AND DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. Both are the same observation in two places: the player's error vocabulary assumes Shaka. They are separate tasks because they have different consumers -- unavailability is a startup decision the controller makes before any source is loaded, while a playback error is a per-attempt outcome the failover scheduler classifies -- and because merging them would put one review range across two behaviours. Whoever takes the second should read the first's verdict. DO NOT BREAK THE FAILOVER CLASSIFICATION. packages/media-engine consumes playback failures and treats network_transient as the only retryable class; an unavailability reason that leaks into that path as retryable would make the player retry a library that is not installed.
review.acceptance: The engine-unavailable vocabulary can represent a native engine failing to load without naming Shaka, a browser or libmpv in the member itself, and the existing web reasons keep their present meaning and their present tests. An engine's own detail is carried beside the reason rather than encoded in it. No unavailability reason reaches the failover scheduler as retryable. The rename or widening is proven by a regression that fails if browser_unsupported is reintroduced as the only way to say an engine is missing.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck --force at integrated head a074b986e899ba8b91d018c4bb71f8c12089b608, exit 0, 9 of 9 and 0 cached. Three of the nine mutation checks are compile-time: widening code to number|null, admitting EOF as a failure reason, and flattening the fault so a code is readable without narrowing each produce tsc exit 2.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at integrated head a074b986e899ba8b91d018c4bb71f8c12089b608, exit 0, 15 of 15 and 0 cached, 2172 passed; 16 new cases, web suite 759 to 775 in its own worktree. THE ENGINE-SPECIFIC CODE IS NOT A FIELD BESIDE A TAG, IT IS INSIDE A VARIANT THE TAG UNLOCKS: a tag alone leaves error.code readable without anyone consulting it, while a discriminated union makes the narrow mandatory and the wrong read a build failure. Three independent barriers keep an mpv number off the classified fields -- code is typed as the literal null on the native variant, fault is a union so an unnarrowed read does not compile, and dispatch narrows on engine so the Shaka classifier cannot receive a native error. Mutation M4 is the one worth reading: it takes TWO simultaneous mutations to make an mpv 6 come back as rights_unverifiable, and the first barrier catches it alone. THE NATIVE BRANCH CLASSIFIES NOTHING AND THAT IS THE ANSWER RATHER THAN A STUB: stop and redirect are taken by aborted a branch up, what remains is an mpv error with no honest table, and the http-status branch was deliberately NOT written even though it would be engine-neutral, because mpv surfaces no HTTP status and the only way to produce one is parsing FFmpeg's English error text, which the failover contract forbids. PL-0204's approval turned on the budget being honest about what it could not classify. BOTH TEST FILES ARE APPEND-ONLY: git diff shows 149 and 90 insertions and ZERO deleted lines, so every pre-existing Shaka regression passes unmodified.

review.title: Playback errors carry an origin, so a native failure is not a Shaka number
review.description: PlaybackError in apps/web/src/components/player/shaka-error.ts carries code and category pinned to Shaka 5.2.x numbering. A native adapter has no such numbers: libmpv reports MPV_EVENT_END_FILE with a reason and an error field, on an entirely different scale. Today a NativePlayerAdapter must either report null in both fields, which discards the only diagnostic it has, or borrow a Shaka number that means something else, which is worse. PL-0901 requires the adapter boundary to expose recoverable and fatal errors without leaking an engine type, and this is where that leaks.
review.notes: AN ORIGIN, SO THE NUMBER MEANS SOMETHING. The proposal the desktop document records is that an error names the engine that produced it, and that its engine-specific code is read only in that origin's terms. The reviewer should also rule on whether the classification the failover scheduler consumes -- rights, decode, source_unavailable, network_transient -- stays engine-neutral and is derived per origin, which is the shape that keeps packages/media-engine from learning about either engine. AN HONEST CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED BEFORE IT IS DISCOVERED. mpv's END_FILE error is coarser than Shaka's code pairs, so a native origin will legitimately classify to unknown more often. The scheduler already handles that: an unclassified charged attempt cannot silently reset the budget, and attemptsByCandidate and attempt_failed_unclassified exist for exactly this. Do not manufacture a false classification to avoid the unknown branch -- PL-0204's approval turned on the budget being honest about what it could not classify. COUPLED TO PL-0903, SEPARATE FOR THE REASON RECORDED THERE.
review.acceptance: A playback error names the origin that produced it, and an engine-specific code is interpretable only against that origin rather than being read on one engine's numbering. A native error can be represented without borrowing a Shaka code and without discarding the detail the engine did supply. The classification packages/media-engine consumes stays engine-neutral, derived per origin, and unchanged in meaning for every existing Shaka case, proven by the existing shaka-error regressions continuing to pass unmodified. An error that cannot be classified stays unclassified rather than being assigned a plausible class.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

recommended.title: Provider health contract
recommended.acceptance: A provider with zero observations reports unknown with a null observed success rate and a zero sample count, never a mid-range score and never a pass; any prior used to rank an unobserved provider is labelled as a prior rather than presented as measured availability; degraded-but-usable is a state distinct from up and down; health output is pure over the observations plus an explicit policy version, with no hidden wall-clock decay; and health never affects entitlement, so a provider at perfect health still cannot make an unauthorized candidate eligible

Created from gpt-architect's round-44 non-blocking finding on PL-0501, in the reviewer's own words: "Create a provider-owned task for the fixture provider protection fact. The fixture adapter, not PL-0501, should emit { state: \"clear\" } when that fact is genuinely known. PL-0501 may keep PROTECTION_NOT_STATED as the conservative fallback until that provider task lands." So the deliverable is a narrowing of where the fact is asserted, not a behaviour change in routing: PROTECTION_NOT_STATED stays in PL-0501 as the fallback for every adapter that has not stated a protection fact, and this task removes the fixture from the set that needs it. Required, and each is a way this task could be done wrongly: the fixture must set the field itself rather than PL-0501 special-casing the fixture provider id, because a consumer branching on a provider identity is exactly the provider-specific logic outside @liberty/provider-sdk that invariant 3 forbids; requiresContentDecryptionModule must be observed returning false for a fixture candidate and the observation recorded, since state !== "clear" is the whole point of the encoding and an untested clear is indistinguishable from an untested unknown; the fallback path in PL-0501 must be left in place and a test must still cover an adapter that states nothing, because deleting the fallback once its only current user stops needing it would fail open for the next adapter; and no other adapter may be given a protection fact here, because for a real provider the honest value is unknown and asserting clear for one would be a rights misstatement rather than a defaulting decision. Out of scope: any change to contract shape (PL-0902 owns it), to ranking (@liberty/media-engine), or to capability routing.
